html:
SMTO-SKL-0135 — Your Slack workspace doesn't allow this action

GUID: 29ac4e1d-3881-50f0-85b6-038ce433c094
Slug: slack-access-denied
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Slack blocked the request because of your workspace's rules or the connected account's access. Slack didn't carry it out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO is connected as your own Slack account, try the same thing yourself in Slack. If it's connected as a bot, skip this step. If Slack blocks you too, the limit is a workspace rule, not an SMTO problem.
  2. Ask your Slack workspace admin to allow the action, or to give that account access to the channel or file. Only Slack admins can change these rules; SMTO has no way around them.
  3. After access is granted, ask the Agent for your request again. Slack refused without acting, so it's safe to repeat once access is allowed.

What success looks like

  • The request completes in Slack.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to your Slack workspace admin. Don't connect a different Slack account just to get around the rule.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack denied the operation with HTTP 403 or the reason no_permission, restricted_action or ekm_access_denied.

What this means

  • Slack returns HTTP 403 or API reasons no_permission, restricted_action or ekm_access_denied. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns HTTP 403 or API reasons no_permission, restricted_action or ekm_access_denied.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected principal, membership, scopes and specific workspace restriction.

How to fix it

  • Check workspace admin policy (including Enterprise Key Management restrictions), the profile's granted_scopes, and the principal's channel or file membership; SMTO provides no administrative bypass or principal substitution.
  • Check workspace policy, scopes and selected principal membership; no administrative bypass is provided.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual permission requirement is met without administrative bypass.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
